incidents.victim: Uber, Revolut, and Rockstar Games (Grand Theft Auto VI developer)
incidents.vector: A British teenager used a hacked Amazon Fire Stick plugged into a hotel room TV to breach the internal systems of Uber, Revolut, and Rockstar Games in September 2022.
incidents.impact: The attacker leaked internal Grand Theft Auto VI development footage and stole data from Uber and Revolut; he was sentenced to seven years on Nov. 24 but released immediately due to time already served in psychiatric detention.

incidents.vector: Suspect allegedly stole payment card and personal data from shopping websites using malware and sold it on criminal forums.
incidents.impact: A hard drive in the suspect's possession held 2.7 million stolen payment card numbers; he was extradited from Kosovo to face an eight-count indictment in Wisconsin.

incidents.vector: Company is investigating a breach that it says appears to have been caused by an AI tool.
incidents.impact: Bell Canada has not disclosed the scope of data affected; the investigation is ongoing.

incidents.vector: Audio/video transcription provider left customer data, including law enforcement body camera transcripts, exposed online.
incidents.impact: Sensitive law enforcement transcription data was publicly accessible before discovery.

incidents.victim: Financial services, healthcare, and legal organizations (US, UK, Australia)
incidents.vector: Com-affiliated actors vish employees posing as IT support to steal credentials and MFA approvals via adversary-in-the-middle proxies, then exfiltrate Microsoft 365/OneDrive/SharePoint data; one cluster also deploys a malicious browser extension disguised as Google Chrome for keylogging and remote control.
incidents.impact: Victims have had tens of millions of CRM and patient records stolen, with attackers broadcasting extortion demands via Teams/email and directing victims to Tor negotiation sites.

incidents.vector: Unattributed espionage group maintained access inside fragmented state administration networks for at least five years, evading detection due to lack of integrated monitoring.
incidents.impact: Tens of millions of government documents were stolen before the intrusion was discovered and the group evicted.

incidents.victim: EU politicians and law enforcement officials
incidents.vector: Pro-Kremlin hacktivist group NoName057(16) published personal information obtained on high-profile individuals, including the Eurojust president, Europol's cybercrime chief, and journalists who cover Russian hacking.
incidents.impact: 18 EU officials and journalists were doxxed; the EU has since moved to sanction the group.

incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote-access service to connect to customer travel routers and IP KVM devices and install a backdoor disguised as a cron process.
incidents.impact: Travel routers and IP KVM devices were backdoored; GL.iNet blocked the attack path and shipped firmware fixes, though infected devices may need a factory reset.

incidents.vector: Company says an attacker used AI tools to breach its systems rapidly.
incidents.impact: 1984 Hosting, Iceland's largest web host and a haven for dissidents worldwide, shut down services to protect customer data, taking tens of thousands of customer sites offline.

incidents.vector: Attacker used authentic credentials leaked by a third party to access the Rackspace Spot cloud marketplace.
incidents.impact: Kubernetes secrets were stolen from customer accounts, and intruders deployed their own pods in affected environments.

incidents.victim: Unibet and other FDJ United platforms
incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against FDJ United's online betting infrastructure.
incidents.impact: FDJ United took down sports-betting platform Unibet and several online casinos; no details on the attack's nature were provided.

incidents.vector: Multiple cyberattacks hit the agency, prompting suspension of all services as a precaution.
incidents.impact: No evidence of data theft found; IMT is the fourth Portuguese government body targeted by cyberattacks in recent weeks.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against the European Commission's internal HR platform.
incidents.impact: Breach disclosed with no further technical details made public.

incidents.victim: Mr. Cooper (Nationstar Mortgage) customers; Rocket Mortgage
incidents.vector: Threat actors impersonated Mr. Cooper employees on calls to trick the IT help desk into issuing temporary passwords, bypassing MFA.
incidents.impact: Large amounts of private customer data were stolen in the November 2023 breach; NY DFS fined Rocket Mortgage (which later acquired Mr. Cooper) $6.75 million combined for MFA, risk-assessment, and incident-reporting failures.

incidents.victim: Federal Bureau of Investigation (National Crime Information Center)
incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into the FBI's NCIC database of warrants, fugitives, and investigation records shared across law enforcement.
incidents.impact: Breach under investigation; the FBI's second major incident this year after the ShinyHunters breach of its HR/recruitment site in September, which stole employee records.

incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a bug in the Entra Connect Health API, introduced by a July update, to scrape tenant configuration data.
incidents.impact: Administrator emails and tenant configuration data were collected before Microsoft deployed a fix.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency holders, gaming-platform account owners, and VoIP software users (Europe)
incidents.vector: Suspected North Korea-aligned group distributes a Go-based 'Overlord' remote access trojan and a Python-based infostealer via lure files impersonating Viber and MicroSIP VoIP software and financial statements, mainly targeting European victims.
incidents.impact: The RAT resists takedown using a kernel-level crash trigger and derives C2 server addresses from Solana blockchain transaction memos; a multi-cryptocurrency clipboard hijacker is also deployed to steal funds.

incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a vulnerability in the 'Classic' tier of Azure API Management to access tokens, passwords, and other credentials stored in the platform; Microsoft later confirmed the flaw also affected the Developer, Basic, Standard, and Premium tiers.
incidents.impact: Both energy firms detected attacks targeting credentials; Equinor's internal services were disrupted (oil and gas production unaffected) and it took until Nov. 20 to fully contain the intrusion, while Norwegian authorities warned the flaw affects organizations across sectors and countries.

incidents.victim: ~700 French retail stores, butchers, food factories, and a slaughterhouse
incidents.vector: IRGC's Shahid Kaveh military cyber unit hacked commercial refrigeration systems, causing freezer failures.
incidents.impact: The October attack caused tens of millions of euros in losses across roughly 700 sites; French officials, in a joint report from five agencies, attributed it to Iran on Nov. 17.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations (including BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger, Zoom, and other media, technology, and financial services brands using Optimizely)
incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a flaw in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer accounts, served from Optimizely's legitimate CDN under its own certificate; the payload was rebuilt 26 times over the day.
incidents.impact: For about 16 hours, 178+ sites served code that swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed payment card data, took screenshots, and attempted to deliver iOS/iPadOS zero-click exploit kits (DarkSword, Coruna); researchers estimate only about $7,500 in crypto was stolen before Optimizely patched the flaw and remediated affected accounts.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against the fundraising platform.
incidents.impact: DonorPerfect took systems offline and has not clarified whether customer or donor data was stolen while gradually restoring service.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against the specialty retailer.
incidents.impact: The company says it has recovered its systems following the attack.

incidents.vector: USDA's security team discovered a breach affecting applications used to issue payments to American farmers.
incidents.impact: Payment applications have been offline for more than a week while IT staff reset passwords across all databases.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupted an IT platform Nissan repair shops use to diagnose vehicles, initially mistaken for a technical outage.
incidents.impact: Repair shops have been unable to diagnose cars, ship firmware fixes, or replace key fobs since Nov. 13.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a ministry website operated by an external service provider between Nov. 12-13.
incidents.impact: Names and official contact details of ministry staff in Vienna and abroad were accessed; the ministry says the breach was contained with no public data compromised, and has not attributed the attack despite the ministry's history of being targeted by Russia-linked hackers.

incidents.vector: Files on the agency's file-sharing service were left exposed online due to a configuration issue.
incidents.impact: Government files were publicly accessible for three and a half months (Jul. 30–Nov. 12) before discovery.

incidents.victim: Government ministries in one Middle Eastern country and four Southeast Asian countries
incidents.vector: A browser-based C2 framework called Falcon compromised government webmail portals and web applications, sideloading malicious Chrome extensions to steal passwords, emails, session cookies, and communications.
incidents.impact: Between March and May 2026, the campaign compromised ministries of foreign affairs, defense, and interior, and law enforcement agencies, consistent with strategic intelligence-collection objectives; a related implant, Antino, used Microsoft OneDrive as a covert C2 channel.

incidents.vector: A shared third-party provider was breached, exposing limited data belonging to customers of all three financial firms.
incidents.impact: Breaches claimed by extortion group 'n0n'; companies describe the exposed data as limited in scope.

incidents.victim: Executive Office of the President (White House network)
incidents.vector: Multiple White House staff devices ran residential-proxy SDKs embedded in free mobile/desktop apps, which rent out a device's internet connection to paying customers; researchers found 28 separate proxy services able to exit through the White House's dedicated IP network.
incidents.impact: Over about a month, proxy traffic exited the White House network 236 times via six IP addresses, exposing a sensitive government network as a rentable exit node for anonymous, unvetted third-party internet traffic.

incidents.vector: Attacker compromised a DevOps engineer's laptop, reached a service container, and submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions, draining about $6.3 billion in under four hours.
incidents.impact: More than $6 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen; Circle froze nearly all the stolen USDC within an hour, while Bitcoin, XRP, and Solana losses largely stand; the US has frozen, seized, or returned over $2.9 billion to date, including a $1.1 billion civil forfeiture action against stolen USDC announced Nov. 23.

incidents.victim: Universities across East Asia (outside mainland China)
incidents.vector: A China-linked actor used autonomous Cairn AI agents, discovering a zero-day in an exposed medical imaging application and gaining root access to a server in about 11 minutes.
incidents.impact: The roughly 48-hour campaign also included unsuccessful attempts against a Redis instance and over 30,000 SSH credential combinations; Amazon Threat Intelligence assesses the agents operated largely without human direction.

incidents.victim: 19 organizations across semiconductor manufacturing, U.S. defense policy, and civil society
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers ran 25 autonomous operations using the open-source Cairn AI pentesting framework paired with Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek models, given only a target and a goal.
incidents.impact: Ten organizations were compromised, including exposure of over one million records at a teachers' union, theft of dozens of valid credentials, and creation of persistent admin accounts and an API token in a semiconductor company's production system.
